✅ English Content (GPT page)

Title: Alireza Kaveh GPT – A Personalized AI for Film Genre Theory and Iranian Cinema

Welcome to the official GPT developed by Alireza Kaveh, Iranian film theorist, author, and director.
This AI assistant is designed to support researchers, cinephiles, students, and educators in navigating complex issues of genre theory, cinematic tone, narrative ideology, and the structure of Iranian cinema.

Kaveh's GPT is built on the foundation of over thirty years of theoretical and practical experience in cinema. As the author of The Film Genre: Tone and Ideology and Seven Genres of Cinema, Kaveh has developed a unique approach to categorizing, analyzing, and interpreting film narratives, particularly within the Iranian cinematic tradition. His emphasis on “tone” and “value systems” in film has reshaped genre theory to account for emotional and ideological depth.

🎯 What This GPT Can Do

Unlike generic chatbots, this GPT has been fine-tuned to:

  • Analyze cinematic tone across different genres
  • Help classify films based on narrative intention rather than just surface elements
  • Answer questions about Kaveh’s genre taxonomy (including emotional tone, ideology, and genre traditions)
  • Provide advice for screenwriters on structure and genre alignment
  • Discuss major trends in Iranian cinema and how they relate to global cinematic movements
  • Assist with academic inquiries related to film studies and cultural tone theory

Whether you're writing a screenplay, analyzing a scene, or researching genre evolution in world cinema, this AI can act as your personal advisor — powered by Kaveh’s theoretical framework.

🧠 Built on Real Scholarship

The GPT draws directly from Kaveh’s academic writings and public lectures. It reflects his five-category cinematic taxonomy — including Medium, Style, Genre, Format, and Tradition — and provides nuanced answers on genre tone, the viewer’s emotional positioning, and value narratives in film.

In particular, it can:

  • Differentiate between genre and style (e.g., musical vs. tragic tone)
  • Interpret viewer engagement (e.g., irony, sincerity, distance)
  • Offer cross-cultural comparisons between Iranian, Bollywood, and Western genre systems

This is not a replacement for human interpretation, but a supportive tool grounded in decades of rigorous thought.

🌍 Why Iranian Cinema? Why GPT?

Iranian cinema often resists traditional Western genre definitions. Alireza Kaveh’s GPT aims to bridge this gap, allowing users to understand how Iranian films engage tone, ideology, and symbolic structure — and how these might be integrated into a broader genre framework.

This GPT is particularly suited to:

  • Film theory students in non-Western contexts
  • Iranian cinema scholars
  • Screenwriters exploring cross-genre narratives
  • Teachers designing cinema-focused syllabi
  • Critics and bloggers seeking genre-based insight

📚 Based on These Works

This GPT reflects the ideas presented in:

  • The Film Genre: Tone and Ideology
  • Seven Genres of Cinema (Vol. 1–3)
  • Such a Dark Mirror (on cinematic reflection and noir sensibility)

You can read more about these books here.
